title: Latency Drift Sentinel — composite latency & network-fingerprint region selector with tier-aware model fallback
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a lightweight "Latency Drift Sentinel" service that fuses short-window p50/p95 latency signatures with packet-loss and jitter fingerprints to generate a composite POP health score. Use the score for region selection and to trigger tier-aware fallback to compatible model variants when needed. The sentinel is intended to reduce noisy cross-POP failovers during transient network events and to keep escalation to higher-cost variants conservative. Core constraints: minimal added latency on the request path, deterministic decisioning for reproducibility, and respect for customer pinning/affinity policies.
acceptance_criteria: Decision latency for region selection (sentinel scoring + routing) must be <= 50 microseconds on the hot path with measured CPU overhead < 3% at 2000 RPS/core
In chaos testing (regional packet loss spike + jitter injection) composite-score based routing must reduce incorrect cross-POP failovers by >= 30% compared to baseline p95-only policy
Fallback to a compatible model variant must honor customer model pins and only choose higher-cost variants when composite-score indicates sustained degradation >30s
Canary rollout (5% traffic) exhibits no regression in 95th percentile end-to-end latency for 95% of routes over 24h
Telemetry emitted: per-POP p50, p95, packet-loss-rate, jitter-ms, composite_score, decision_reason (string) — all visible in Console dashboard and exported to Prometheus
comments: 2026-02-10 Aisha Patel: Created initial ticket after post-mortem of INC-2026-02 where a transient cross-pop network spike caused cascading variant escalation. Proposed composite scoring instead of p95-only to reduce sensitivity to short-lived outliers.

2026-02-17 Marco Chen: Spike prototype implemented: sliding-window (30s) p50/p95 + EWMA packet-loss. Early sims show fewer failovers but some delayed detection of true POP outages. Trade-off: shorter windows are reactive but noisy; longer windows smooth but delay failover. Proposal: dual-window strategy (short window for anomaly detection + medium window for confirmation).

2026-02-25 Design review (Sofia Martinez): UX constraints — Console needs to surface 'decision_reason' with human-readable labels. Also request an explainer tooltip for customers about why their requests moved to fallback variants.

2026-03-02 Performance bench (Marco): Bench on c6i-like instance at 2k RPS/core shows scoring adds ~35ns per request in the hot path when implemented in C++ core; Python shim for rollout is ~1.8us — decision: implement sentinel core in Rust/C++ and expose flag for progressive rollout.

2026-03-08 PM sync (Liam O'Connor): We must ensure customer pinned-models never get auto-swapped; instead route to alternate POPs or degrade to best-effort with explicit notification. Added acceptance criterion to honor pins.

2026-03-12 Marco Chen: Submitted initial RFC and canary plan. PR #8123 opened for runtime integration (link in attachments). Next: create load and chaos experiment in staging, add Prometheus exporters, and prepare canary rollout docs.
notes: Trade-offs considered: (1) p95-only thresholding (fast but brittle), (2) full causal network model (accurate but heavyweight), (3) composite lightweight fingerprint (selected).
Rollout plan: unit tests -> staging canary (5%) -> expand to 25% with rollback thresholds -> full rollout. Rollback on >1.5x increase in observed tail-latency or >0.5% customer errors.
Open questions: how to weight p50 vs p95 for mixed traffic profiles; whether to include TCP retransmit counts (requires kernel hooks) or rely on packet-loss probe metrics.
